title: std::cout
description:
---
In C++, to print to console, two things are neccesary. First, you must import iostram. at the very top of the file, 
`#include <iostream>`. this imports the standard library's console input/output library. The way you actually print is by typing `std::cout` followed by the output operator `<<` then either a variable(which will be coverd later) or a number/ string, so for a string you put quotes and then want you want to type, like "text" then a semicolon. All statments in C++ end in ;. After you have your text, you can also output an escape squense. An escape sequence is a special series of charecters that does things. `\n` is a good example. `\n` represents a newline charecter, so after your text before the semicolon, you put `<< '\n';` to type a newline. You may be thinking "Why are there single quotes instead of double quotes?". The reason is not a style choice, instead it is that escape squences are not a string, their type is actually a charecter(char). The char data type represents a single ascii charecter, escape sequence, or 4-digit unicode charecter, and all chars are wrapped in single quotes only, nothing else works.

## Assignment
Print to console the exact string "I like C++" followed by a newline.
